newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer spending up 4.5 pct this year - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer spending up 4.5 pct this year - Brown.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Wednesday that consumer spending would rise by 4.5 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1998.
"Consumer spending is expected to increase by 4.5 percent this year, is forecast to grow more slowly at four percent next year," he told parliament in his budget speech.

Economists are worried that a flood of windfall payments from building societies converting into banks -- totalling more than 30 billion pounds over the summer -- will fuel an unsustainable high street boom.
In last November's budget, Kenneth Clarke, Brown's predecessor, forecast consumer spending growth of 4.25 percent this year and 3.75 percent in the first half of next year.
(A separate summary of key economic forecasts will run after Brown finishes speaking.)
